recipe.title: Turnip, leek and cheddar quiche
recipe.intro: Early February turnips are small, firm and gently peppery. Softened in butter with leeks, they turn sweet and make a quiche that tastes far richer than it costs.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan, 200°C conventional, with a baking tray on the middle shelf. Line the tart tin with the pastry, letting the excess hang over the edge. Prick the base all over with a fork and chill while you cook the filling.

Melt the butter in the frying pan over a medium heat. Add the turnips, leeks and thyme with a pinch of salt, cover and cook for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the turnips are tender and the leeks soft and sweet.
Meanwhile whisk the eggs, milk, cream and mustard in a jug with most of the cheddar, the rest of the salt and the pepper.
Spread the turnip and leek mixture over the pastry base. Pour in the egg mixture and scatter over the last of the cheese.
Set the tin on the hot baking tray, which helps crisp the base. Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until the filling is golden and set with just a slight wobble in the middle.
Leave to rest for 10 minutes, then trim the overhanging pastry with a sharp knife and lift out of the tin. Serve warm or at room temperature.
recipe.tip: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge and is good cold in lunchboxes. Swede or parsnip work in place of half the turnips.
